title: AT 2024wpp: an extremely luminous fast ultraviolet transient powered by accretion onto a black hole
question: What are the multi-wavelength observational properties, energy source, and progenitor system of the extremely luminous fast ultraviolet transient AT 2024wpp?

what.value: Pre-explosion host galaxy photometry from DECam Legacy Survey, WISE, and GALEX

evidence.quote: Photometry of the host is taken from Legacy Survey Tractor forced photometry on pre-explosion images from DECam in the $griz$ filters, from WISE (cite: Wright+2010) in the (mid-IR) W1 and W2 filters, and from the GALEX archive (cite: Bianchi+2017).

what.value: Light curves, spectra, blackbody parameters, and CSM density profiles of comparison transients (AT 2018cow, CSS161010, AT 2022tsd, MUSSES2020j, SN 2018gep, SN 2020bvc, SN 2008D, SN 2017egm, AT 2019cmw, SN 2021csp, ASASSN-14li, SN 2006jc, SN 2024fyq, SN 2023ixf)

evidence.quote: Data for the comparison objects are obtained from (cite: Perley+2019) (AT 2018cow), (cite: Gutierrez+2024) (CSS161010), (cite: Ho+2023tsd) (AT 2022tsd), and (cite: Jiang+2022) (MUSSES2020j; we apply an approximate extra $k$-correction of 1 mag to convert their observed $r$-band light curve to rest-frame $g$-band).

which compares the COS spectrum of AT 2024wpp to three other fast and luminous blue transients observed with HST at FUV wavelengths: SN 2021csp (Icn, from (cite: Perley+2022)), SN 2023iuc (Ibn), and ASASSN-14li (TDE, from (cite: Cenko+2016)).

external_data.citation: Perley+2019; Gutierrez+2024; Ho+2023tsd; Jiang+2022; Ho+2019; Ho+2020bvc; Modjaz+2009; Zhu+2023; Wise+2026; Perley+2022; Cenko+2016; Maeda+2022; BaerWay+2025; Zimmerman+2024; Coppejans+2020

recipe.goal: Measure radio and millimeter continuum flux densities
recipe.method: Download ALMA QA2 pipeline-calibrated images and report QA2 peak flux density and rms (verified with imtool); reduce VLA data with CASA VLA pipeline and VLA Imaging Pipeline and measure flux density and rms using pwkit/imtool
key_parameters: VLA sub-bands of 0.5 GHz, 1 GHz, or 2 GHz as well as full receiver bandwidth

recipe.goal: Model radio/millimeter SEDs and derive shock and CSM properties
recipe.method: Fit a soft broken power-law to radio+ALMA SEDs at six epochs (30, 41, 66, 103, 119, 177 rest-frame days) to find peak flux and peak frequency, then infer shock radius, magnetic field, total energy, shock speed, and ambient electron density using synchrotron self-absorption (SSA) equations
key_parameters: Factor of 1.37 correction applied to 27d X and Ku measurements in first epoch SED
assumptions: Nonthermal power-law electron energy distribution with p = 3, volume filling factor f = 0.5, and equipartition epsilon_B = epsilon_e = 1/3
10% overall flux calibration uncertainty and interstellar scintillation modulations included

recipe.goal: Construct UVOIR light curves and fit blackbody evolution
recipe.method: Perform image subtraction and forced/aperture/PSF photometry across UVOIR facilities, apply empirical filter offsets and Galactic extinction correction, interpolate light curves using polynomial fits and local regression, and fit Planck functions to co-eval SEDs from 2 to 111 rest-frame days
key_parameters: 10% systematic error term included in SED fits; PS1 y-band after 16 rest-frame days excluded
assumptions: Cosmology: Omega_M = 0.3, Omega_Lambda = 0.7, H_0 = 70 km s^-1 Mpc^-1; Galactic E(B-V) = 0.026 mag; zero host extinction

recipe.goal: Analyze X-ray spectrum and light curve
recipe.method: Extract Swift/XRT count rates using Swift team online tools, fit a power-law spectrum to the first ten days of observations, and convert count rates to unabsorbed 0.3-10 keV fluxes using WebPIMMS
key_parameters: Conversion factor = 4.865e-11 erg cm^-2 per count
assumptions: Milky Way N_H = 2.7e20 cm^-2 and intrinsic host N_H = 6.3e20 cm^-2

recipe.goal: Analyze UV and optical spectroscopy of transient
recipe.method: Reduce ground-based and HST COS/STIS spectra, rescale to interpolated photometry, measure narrow ISM absorption equivalent widths via Gaussian fits or direct integration, fit damped Lyman-alpha profile, and measure late-time H and He emission line profiles
key_parameters: UV+optical spectrum binned to R approx 200 (1400 km s^-1)

recipe.goal: Derive host galaxy physical properties from SED and IFU spectroscopy
recipe.method: Fit UV-to-MIR host galaxy photometry with prospector (using FSPS and dynesty) after removing nebular line contributions, and fit Gaussian profiles to continuum-subtracted KCWI IFU emission lines to derive Balmer decrement, SFR, and gas-phase metallicity
key_parameters: 7 arcsec radius aperture for VLT, NTT, and UVOT host photometry; 2x FWHM elliptical aperture for KCWI host spectrum
assumptions: Chabrier IMF, Calzetti dust attenuation model, delayed-tau SFH (t * exp(-t/tau)), fixed stellar metallicity log(Z/Z_sun) = -0.6 from mass-metallicity relation

evidence.quote: From integrating the bolometric light curve, we infer a total radiated energy of $1.0\times10^{51}\,$erg.

answer_key.quantity: X-ray photon index (first 10 days)

evidence.quote: We found that the data are well described by a power law with index $\Gamma=1.7^{+0.3}_{-0.3}$ (90% confidence).

answer_key.quantity: Host galaxy damped Lyman-alpha neutral hydrogen column density

evidence.quote: The broad Lyman-$\alpha$ feature (the blue wing of which is cut off by geocoronal contamination) is well-fit by a damped Lyman-$\alpha$ profile and indicates a hydrogen column through the host of (6.5 $\pm$ 0.4) $\times$ $10^{20}$ cm$^{-2}$.

answer_key.quantity: Late-time H and He blueshifted emission component velocity offset

evidence.quote: the H$\alpha$ line in particular shows a clear double-peaked profile, with one component peaking at or near the systemic redshift and another peaking at a relative blueshift of $\Delta v = -$6600 km s$^{-1}$.

evidence.loc: Constraints on the rate of 18cow-like and 24wpp-like transients
evidence.quote: Assuming that all LFBOTs in this volume were successfully classified, this corresponds to a rate (95% confidence interval) of 0.9–12.5 yr$^{-1}$ Gpc$^{-3}$, or about 0.001–0.01% of the core-collapse supernova rate ($10^5$ yr$^{-1}$ Gpc$^{-3}$; (cite: Perley+2020)).

score_reason: All ALMA and VLA flux densities are explicitly tabulated in Table 4, ALMA measurements come directly from archive QA2 products, and the analytical equations (SSA from Chrimes+2024b, diffusion mass, X-ray ionization criteria from Govreen-Segal+2025) are fully specified, though custom fitting scripts are not released.
rediscovery_reason: ALMA QA2 continuum images are directly available in the ALMA archive under 2023.1.01730.T, all radio/mm flux densities are tabulated, and the broken power-law SSA shock parameter derivations and UVOIR blackbody fits have clear numerical answer keys.
